title: A nest in a tree
hook: Compare the effects on both participants.

knows: Ecological interactions can affect participants differently.
doesNotKnow: The bird benefits and the tree is assumed unaffected, so the stipulated relationship is commensalism. Real effects should be measured rather than assumed.

misconception: An interaction must affect both participants in the same way.
objective: Classify the stated effects of an ecological interaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: A bird gains a nesting site in a tree; assume the tree has no appreciable benefit or harm in this example. Using + for benefit, − for harm and 0 for no appreciable effect, which signs describe Bird and Tree, in that order? Bird: +; Tree: 0. The bird benefits and the tree is assumed unaffected, so the stipulated relationship is commensalism. Real effects should be measured rather than assumed.
claims.source: Stipulated simplified example; ecological definitions: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-6-community-ecology

claims.text: Icons and signs summarize the stipulated interaction and do not quantify fitness or capture every ecological effect.

Recall: What term describes the Bird–Tree interaction as stated in the lesson? The bird benefits and the tree is assumed unaffected, so the stipulated relationship is commensalism. Real effects should be measured rather than assumed.
